subject: Post-call: PulseWorks SDK adaptor and streaming-fallback recap
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@pulseworks.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PulseWorks SDK adaptor and streaming-fallback recap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we keep momentum.

High-level pain points you shared
- Incumbent latency spikes at peak usage (95th pct > 800ms for single-shot generation)
- Need to support streaming token delivery for live transcription features and progressive UI
- Reranking candidate lists using embeddings + semantic similarity to improve suggestions
- Strict audit/logging requirements for HIPAA-adjacent workflows (retention + access logs)

Goals you want to hit in Q4
1) 200ms median latency on inference paths for user-facing responses
2) Streaming-first SDK support for browser + mobile clients
3) A rerank pipeline using embeddings to reduce false positives by 20–30%

What we propose
- SDK change: add streaming WebSocket endpoint + client helpers for incremental decode and func-calls
- Structured outputs: a JSON-first mode (schema validation + soft failover) to make downstream parsing deterministic
- Rerank: an embeddings-based shortlist (128-d vector) with a lightweight ANN index served alongside primary model
- Compliance: supply audit logs and an exportable retention policy; we'll work with your security contact on evidence pack (SOC2 + infra diagrams)

Immediate next steps
- Marcus to run a short perf test plan with a sample payload you provide (we'll need 1k requests with realistic seq len distribution)
- Alex / Kai: share sample request payloads and a short list of 3 critical UI flows by Friday 9/10
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) for API walkthrough + integration checklist

Attachments: pulseworks_prod_requirements.pdf (requirements), pulseworks_terms_draft.docx (initial commercial terms)

Thanks — I'm looping Ben for implementation questions. If that all looks correct, we'll lock in the deep-dive time.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@pulseworks.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PulseWorks SDK adaptor and streaming-fallback recap

Irene —

Appreciate the concise recap, this matches our notes. A couple clarifications:
- Our 95th pct latency currently hits ~1.2s under peak (>5k rps), so your 200ms median target sounds ambitious but we want to see tradeoffs (quantization / smaller model tier)
- Streaming must support function-calls: we need the model to emit structured events (e.g., {"action":"suggest","payload":{...}}) while still being able to stream tokens to the UI
- For rerank, we can provide a candidate pool export (CSV of ~50k items) and an initial labeling set of 2k pairs

I've attached an internal network topology snapshot (pulseworks_arch.png) and copied our security lead Kai Rivera (kai.rivera@pulseworks.ai) to start the compliance thread.

Available slots for the deep-dive: Mon 9/7 11:00–12:00 PT or Tue 9/8 09:00–10:00 PT. We prefer a labeled test harness from Redwood that we can run on our infra.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, PulseWorks
alex.dunn@pulseworks.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@pulseworks.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PulseWorks SDK adaptor and streaming-fallback recap

Alex — thanks for the details and the topology diagram. Quick replies to the bullets and proposed plan:

- Latency: we'll prepare a two-tier plan: (A) configure a quantized 8-bit path with aggressive batching for background tasks and (B) a lower-latency FP16 streaming path for user-facing responses. We'll include perf estimates for both.
- Streaming + function-calls: we can support token-streaming with interleaved structured events. Proposal: define a lightweight event envelope ("redwood_event") that can contain either partial tokens or a JSON function payload; we'll share a sample contract in the deep-dive.
- Rerank: Marcus will take the candidate export and propose an ANN index config (HNSW params) and retrieval latency/accuracy tradeoffs.

Action items we own
- Marcus: prepare the integration checklist + sample WebSocket client by Tue 9/8
- Ben: deliver perf plan and cost estimate by Wed 9/9
- Irene: coordinate compliance kickoff with Kai and collect their evidence list

I've also created a HubSpot deal (PW-2026-089) and linked a shared drive folder. DocuSign NDA link is below if you'd like to get legal started before the deep-dive.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/contract/PW-NDA-2026
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/39284753
Drive: https://redwood.app/s/drive/pulseworks/arch-diagram

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@pulseworks.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kai Rivera <kai.rivera@pulseworks.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PulseWorks SDK adaptor and streaming-fallback recap

Thanks all — locking in Mon 9/7 11:00 PT for the deep-dive (calendar invite sent). Alex/Kai: please drop the sample payloads and the 3 UI flows to the Drive folder before EOD 9/6 so Marcus can start drafting tests.

I'll bring the sample WebSocket client and the first-draft event envelope to the call.

—Irene
